item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web: Updated search experience with Copilot Search
item.description:
[What and why]

We are updating the search experience in SharePoint Online and OneDrive on the web to align with the Copilot Search experience across Microsoft 365. This updated experience allows users to search using natural-language prompts and combines relevant search results, AI-generated summaries with source references, and filters. By bringing SharePoint and OneDrive onto a common search interface, we are providing a more consistent and familiar search experience across Microsoft 365.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Frontier Preview (Worldwide): Rollout began in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-January 2027.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-January 2027 and is expected to complete by mid-April 2027.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who search for content in SharePoint Online and OneDrive on the web

Platforms and services

  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive on the web

What will happen

  • Users will see a modernized search experience aligned with Copilot Search across Microsoft 365. Please note that, while the core experience is shared, some AI-powered capabilities are available based on licensing.
  • SharePoint Online and OneDrive on the web will use a common search interface, providing a more consistent experience regardless of where users begin their search.
  • During the Frontier Preview period, SharePoint Online and OneDrive on the web will provide an opt-out option if users determine a critical search feature they rely on is unavailable.

Modernized search experiences in SharePoint and OneDrive

[Action required and recommendations]

No significant deployment work is required. We recommend that you test any custom search experiences or integrations that may be affected by the updated search experience. If your organization needs more time to prepare for this change, options are available to defer the new experience at the tenant and individual site level.

[Learn more]

We will publish new documentation prior to General Availability release.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: New chat sections for muted and meeting chats
item.description:
Updated November 5, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[Introduction]

Microsoft Teams is introducing two new system chat sections called Muted chats and Meeting chats. These sections allow users to organize their chat and channels list by grouping muted conversations and meeting chats into dedicated sections that users can turn on or off. The new Meeting chats section will replace the Meeting chats filter, that was previously available at the top of the chat and channel list.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 559605.

[When this will happen]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout begins in early January 2027 (previously early November 2026) (previously mid-October) and is expected to complete by late January 2027 (previously mid-November 2026).

[How this affects your organization]

Who is affected

  • All Microsoft Teams users in Microsoft 365 tenants, including Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD

What will happen

Users may see up to two new system sections in their Teams chat and channels list:

  • Muted chats section
    • Enabled by default.
    • Muted chats that are not in Favorites or user‑created sections automatically move to this section.
    • The section appears at the bottom of the chat list.
    • Unread chats continue to appear bold.
  • Meeting chats section
    • Disabled by default.
    • When enabled by the user, meeting chats that are not in Favorites or user‑created sections automatically move to this section.
    • The section appears below the main chats list.
    • Unread chats continue to appear bold and contribute to badge counts.
  • Chats in Favorites or user‑created sections are not moved.
  • Users can drag and drop these sections to reorder them.
  • There are no admin controls for these sections.

[What you can do to prepare]

No admin action is required.

You may want to:

  • Inform users that new chat sections are available and that they can turn them on or off.
  • Notify helpdesk staff that muted chats may appear in a separate section by default.
  • Direct users to Settings > Chats and channels to manage these sections.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Automatically add tag members to channels with Workflows
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing the Join member to channel when user is added to tag template in the Workflows app to automatically add users to selected channels when they are added to a team tag. Once configured, the workflow runs whenever a user is added to the tag, eliminating the need to add members to each channel manually. This is especially useful for location-based or project-based groups where tags correspond to specific sites, regions, or projects, helping new members access relevant channels promptly.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams users who are added to team tags associated with configured workflows.
  • Team owners who choose to configure the workflow.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Workflows app
  • Power Automate

What will happen

  • The Join member to channel when user is added to tag template will be available in the Workflows app.
  • When configured, the workflow will automatically add users to selected channels when they are added to a team tag.
  • Nothing changes by default. The template is optional and does not run until someone in a team configures it.

Joining new tag members to channels

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. If your organization plans to use this template, we recommend reviewing your Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm that it is permitted. Team owners can configure the workflow at any time if desired.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Decline incoming mobile calls with a message
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Teams mobile users will be able to decline an incoming Teams call and send a message to the caller at the same time. This gives users a faster way to communicate their availability without answering the call or separately navigating to chat.

From the incoming call screen, users can select Message and choose a predefined response or select Custom to compose a personalized response in the relevant Teams chat.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams mobile users who receive eligible Teams-to-Teams calls and have an associated Teams chat available for the response

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams mobile

What will happen

Once this feature is available:

  • Users will see a new Message option on the incoming call screen.
  • Users can choose a predefined response, such as “Can I call you later?”, “I’m on my way.”, or “Sorry, I can’t talk right now.”
  • Selecting a predefined response will decline the call and immediately send the selected message to the caller in Teams chat.
  • Users can select Custom to decline the call and open the relevant Teams chat to compose a personalized response.
  • The response will appear in Teams chat so users can continue the conversation after the call is declined.
  • This capability will not apply to PSTN, anonymous, or interoperability calls where there is no corresponding Teams chat to receive the message.
  • Existing options to accept or decline an incoming call will not change.
  • The feature will become available automatically as it rolls out to eligible users.

item.title: [planForChange] Action required: Update permissions for Exchange Online Admin API
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is updating the authorization model for Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 by introducing dedicated API permissions. This change provides a clearer permission model for applications accessing Exchange Online administrative endpoints and supports the ongoing modernization of Exchange Online administration, including migration from Exchange Web Services (EWS).

The Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 endpoints are not being retired. Only the permissions used to access them are changing:

  • Exchange.ManageV2 is being replaced by Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage.
  • Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 is being replaced by Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp.

Applications using the affected permissions must transition to the corresponding new permissions to maintain uninterrupted access.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: New permissions become available November 1, 2026. Complete migration by November 30, 2026. Existing permissions are deprecated December 1, 2026.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: Rollout begins in November 2026, with existing permissions deprecated January 1, 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

This change affects organizations that develop, own, or manage applications accessing Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 using Exchange.ManageV2 for delegated access or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 for application-only access. If your organization does not use either permission, no action is required.

Platforms/Services:

  • Exchange Online
  • Exchange Online Admin API v2.0
  • Microsoft Entra application permission and consent configuration

What will happen:

  • Applications must transition to Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage or Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp, as applicable.
  • Administrators must grant consent to the new permissions where required.
  • Existing Exchange Online RBAC requirements continue to apply.
  • Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 endpoint URLs, API version, and supported operations are not changing as a result of this update.
  • Applications relying exclusively on the retired permissions after the applicable deprecation date will no longer be able to access the APIs.

Action Required/Recommendations:

  1. Identify affected applications. Review applications using Exchange.ManageV2 or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2.
  2. Configure the new permissions. Add the corresponding Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage or Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp permission.
  3. Grant administrator consent. Ensure the required new permissions are approved.
  4. Verify Exchange RBAC assignments. Confirm that the application or delegated user has the necessary Exchange roles.
  5. Validate API functionality. Test affected workflows using the new permissions before removing the existing permissions.
  6. Remove the retired permissions. After successful validation, remove the old permissions from the application configuration.
  7. Update explicit permission references. Update configurations, scripts, or consent workflows that reference the existing permission names.
  8. Check third-party applications. Contact your application provider to determine whether an update is required.

For more information, see Authentication and authorization for the Exchange Online Admin API.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Action required: Exchange Online Admin API MailboxFolderPermission response update
item.description:
[What and why:]

Microsoft is updating the Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 MailboxFolderPermission endpoint to return the User property as a structured object instead of a display-name string. The new response includes DisplayName, Name, and PrimarySmtpAddress, helping applications more reliably identify users with similar or identical display names and supporting mailbox folder permission management and EWS migration scenarios.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • Rollout will begin and is expected to complete in early November 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: Organizations with applications or third-party solutions that use the Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 MailboxFolderPermission endpoint and process the User property.

Platforms/Services: Exchange Online Admin API v2.0, specifically the MailboxFolderPermission endpoint.

What will happen:

  • The User property will change from a string to a structured object.
  • The object will contain DisplayName, Name, and PrimarySmtpAddress.
  • The endpoint URL and API version will not change.
  • Applications that expect User to be a string may experience parsing errors or unexpected behavior after the change.
  • Applications can use PrimarySmtpAddress to more reliably distinguish between users with similar display names.

Current response:

{

  "User": "<display name>"

}

New response:

{

  "User": {

    "DisplayName": "...",

    "Name": "...",

    "PrimarySmtpAddress": "..."

  }

}

[Action required/recommendations:]

Action is required if your organization uses the MailboxFolderPermission endpoint and processes the User property. Before rollout:

  • Review applications that read or process the User property.
  • Update response handling to process User as a structured object instead of a string.
  • Where appropriate, use PrimarySmtpAddress to identify the user associated with a mailbox folder permission.
  • Test permission retrieval, user identification, and mailbox folder permission management workflows.
  • Update dependent integrations that store, consume, or forward the User property.
  • If you use a third-party solution that manages mailbox folder permissions, contact the solution provider to determine whether an update is required.
  • For more information, see Exchange Online Admin API overview.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Planner: Planner capabilities in Copilot Cowork through the Planner Plugin
item.description:
[What and why]

The Planner Plugin connects Microsoft Planner to Copilot Cowork, helping users understand their priorities, get help completing tasks, and keep their plans current. Cowork can use Planner task notes, checklists, and attachments to research, draft, analyze, and create deliverables. It can also turn existing content into plans, generate visual status reports, and use Planner context for work across Microsoft 365. Users review and approve changes before Cowork updates Planner.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): We began rolling out in late October 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026.
  • The experience is available now in Frontier, with general availability targeted for November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license, access to Copilot Cowork and Microsoft Planner, and permission to use the Planner Plugin

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Copilot Cowork
  • Microsoft Planner

What will happen

Users can find the Planner Plugin, published by Microsoft Corporation, in Microsoft Copilot under Plugins > Cowork. After the plugin is available and any required account connection is completed, users can:

  • Prioritize work: See assigned tasks across plans, identify overdue and upcoming work, and get recommendations about what to focus on.
  • Get help completing tasks: Use task instructions, checklists, and attachments to research, draft, analyze, or create files. After approval, Cowork can update progress, complete checklist items, add deliverable links, and mark tasks complete.
  • Create plans and tasks from existing content: Turn spreadsheets, documents, presentations, meeting notes, or goals into proposed plans and tasks for review and approval.
  • Generate visual plan reports: Summarize progress, upcoming and overdue tasks, work by owner and bucket, progress toward goals, blockers, and recommended next steps.
  • Work across Microsoft 365: Use Planner context to draft and send emails, schedule meetings, post Teams updates, and create documents, presentations, or spreadsheets. Users review and approve actions before Cowork takes them.
  • Automate recurring work: Schedule task summaries and plan reports, or trigger requests from events such as emails and Teams messages. Changes to Planner still require approval.

Administrators control plugin availability for their organization or for selected users and groups. Admin-deployed plugins are automatically acquired for targeted users. Users can enable or disable acquired plugins for their own Cowork conversations.The plugin acts within the signed-in user's existing Planner permissions and does not grant additional access.

Screenshot 1 - Add the Planner Plugin:

Screenshot 2 - Assigned tasks view:

Screenshot 3 - Task execution view:

[Action required and recommendations]

To prepare:

  • Confirm that intended users have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and access to Copilot Cowork and Microsoft Planner.
  • In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Tools or Agents > All agents, find the Planner Plugin, and install it for the intended users or groups. Alternatively, configure availability so eligible users can acquire it themselves.
  • Direct users to complete any required connector sign-in or consent. Administrators cannot sign in on their behalf.
  • Consider updating your helpdesk and internal user guidance if you plan to make the plugin available.

If the plugin is already deployed to the intended users, no additional deployment action is needed.

Learn more

  • Manage plugins for Copilot Cowork | Microsoft Learn
  • Use plugins with Copilot Cowork | Microsoft Learn
  • What you can do with Planner in Cowork | Microsoft Support

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Copilot Cowork can use existing Planner data, including task notes, checklists, attachments, owners, and due dates, as context for completing work across Microsoft 365. Users review and approve actions before Cowork takes them.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The Planner Plugin enables Copilot Cowork to use Planner context to research, draft, analyze, create deliverables, generate reports, and perform Planner-related actions.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can use Copilot Cowork with the Planner Plugin to prioritize work, complete tasks, create plans and reports, and perform work across Microsoft 365 using Planner context.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Administrators can control availability of the Planner Plugin for the organization or for specific users and groups through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves?Yes. Users can enable or disable an acquired plugin for their own Copilot Cowork conversations through the Sources & Skills panel.

item.title: [stayInformed] Sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot - Semantic model in Sales Agent
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to enable semantic model support for Sales Agent. This feature will reach general availability on November 17, 2026.

How does this affect me?
The semantic model signals help Sales Agent better understand CRM data structure, views, relationships, forms, and business terminology.

Administrators can fine-tune the semantic model signals to include the CRM tables, relationships, views, and glossary terms that Sales Agent can use when grounding responses. This helps improve response quality, especially in environments with custom CRM schemas and complex data relationships.

Sellers can ask questions in Sales Agent using natural language and get answers that better reflect custom CRM tables, relationships, forms, views, and terminology. This helps sellers uncover customer context with more accurate interpretation of CRM data, and it helps admins minimize glossary maintenance.

Existing permissions and administrator-managed data coverage continue to apply.

What action do I need to take?

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Use role-based enforcement for recording and transcription downloads
item.description:
Update: Release of this feature has been postponed; we will announce a new date in the future.

We are announcing the ability to use role-based enforcement for recording and transcription downloads in Dynamics 365 Contact Center.

How does this affect me?
This feature helps organizations better protect sensitive customer communications by separating permissions to view recordings and transcripts from permissions to download them. Admins can assign new Dataverse security roles to prevent selected users from downloading recordings or transcripts while still allowing them to view and play back content as permitted by existing access.

The two new Dataverse security roles that will be available are:
  • Deny Recording Download
  • Deny Transcription Download
When either role is assigned to a user:
  • The user can continue to view and play back recordings and transcripts as permitted by existing access.
  • The user is blocked from downloading the corresponding artifact.
Enforcement of these models is applied server-side across the Dynamics 365 Contact Center UI, public and internal APIs, and direct download URLs or integrations. Download requests will also be denied regardless of how they are initiated.

Access control is driven entirely by Dataverse role assignment. The deny roles override implicit download behavior without affecting recording, transcription, or playback functionality.

These controls help reduce the risk of unauthorized data export, support compliance and data governance requirements, and allow organizations to maintain operational visibility without allowing data removal.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Automate - Information regarding the end of support for Copilot in the designer for cloud flows or agent flows.

item.title: [planForChange] Work IQ expands memory capabilities to agents
item.description:
[What and why]

A new Work IQ MCP path, /memory/me/coreMemories, gives authorized agents access to a user’s memory profile. This profile enables agents to provide more personalized and relevant assistance. At launch, it includes Custom Instructions, Saved Memories, and memories derived from chat history. The memory profile will continue to evolve and improve over time.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026 and expected to complete by late December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users whose agents have access to the Work IQ MCP server and whose applicable personalization settings allow the relevant information to be included in their memory profile

Platforms and services

  • Work IQ MCP
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

A new /memory/me/coreMemoriespath in Work IQ MCP will provide a memory profile for the authenticated user.

The path supports only the fetch tool. Memory cannot be written or modified through Work IQ MCP.

Only the authenticated user’s memory profile is available. A user’s memory profile is not shared with other users.

Work IQ MCP has a new policy that controls access to memory through Work IQ MCP at Microsoft 365 Admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Policies. Like other read policies, this policy is enabled by default.

If Enhanced personalization is disabled, Copilot Memory is disabled and is not available through the MCP path.

  • User personalization settings in Copilot Chat > Settings > Personalization are respected:If Customize Copilot is disabled, Custom Instructions are not included in the memory profile.
  • If Saved memories is disabled, saved memories are not included in the memory profile.
  • If Chat history & work insights is disabled, insights from chat history and Microsoft 365 activity are not included in the memory profile.

Changes to the Enhanced personalization control and to the user settings may take up to 48 hours to take effect.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Admins who want to manage access to memory through Work IQ MCP can review the memory read policy at Microsoft 365 Admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Policies.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Work IQ MCP has a memory read policy under Microsoft 365 Admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Policies. The policy is enabled by default.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Viva Engage: Improved shared message experience

Platforms and services

What will happen

Updated Viva Engage feed experience

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot Chat: Planner Agent task assignment, catch-up, and Copilot memory integration
item.description:
[What and why]

We are expanding Planner Agent in Microsoft Copilot Chat with task assignment, scheduled task catch-up, and Copilot memory integration. These improvements help users manage tasks and shared plans, identify outstanding work, and receive personalized responses. We are also improving support for larger plans, response quality, speed, and reliability.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with an active Microsoft Copilot license who have access to Planner Agent. Administrators can manage Planner Agent availability through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Copilot on the web
  • Microsoft Copilot in Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft Planner

What will happen

Task assignment

  • Users can assign tasks to one or more people in shared basic plans, including assigning multiple tasks at once.
  • Users can reassign or remove assignees, view tasks grouped by person, and review proposed changes before saving them.

Scheduled task catch-up

  • Users can identify outstanding work, commitments, and items awaiting their input based on recent emails, chats, and meetings.
  • Users can generate suggestions on demand or configure recurring schedules with optional email notifications when suggestions are ready for review.
  • Suggested tasks include their sources and remain editable drafts until users save them to Planner. Users can modify, pause, or delete their schedules.

Copilot memory

  • Planner Agent can personalize responses using saved memories and preferences inferred from previous Copilot chats.
  • Users can save, update, or delete memories through Planner Agent and review, delete, or turn off memories in Copilot personalization settings.

Additional improvements

  • Users can create plans without the previous 30-task limit and receive more complete responses for complex plans.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Orchestrate conversation distribution with natural language playbooks
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to orchestrate conversation distribution with natural language playbooks in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will be generally available by November 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Users will be able to configure natural-language playbooks to automatically manage conversation priority, overflow handling, representative assignment, and routing as conditions change throughout the conversation lifecycle.

Key capabilities will include:
  • Dynamic priority escalation: Adjust priority based on wait time, queue transfers, customer tier, and other conditions.
  • Overflow handling: Trigger callbacks, route conversations to alternate queues, expand assignment eligibility, notify supervisors, or send contextual customer messages when defined conditions occur, including for direct inward dial calls.
  • Preferred representative assignment: Reconnect customers with previously engaged or preferred representatives when available and within capacity, with fallback to another qualified representative.
  • Bullseye routing: Expand the pool of eligible representatives over time based on skills, proficiency, teams, or other criteria.
Users will configure playbooks through guided templates with built-in validation to identify conflicts before publication. Publishing a playbook will consume Copilot credits. No Copilot credits will be consumed during runtime when playbooks process conversations.

Existing customers can continue using their current conversation orchestration playbooks, and new customers can create playbooks.

What action do I need to take?
Users will need to enable the conversation orchestration toggle to use this capability. Enabling the toggle will not consume Copilot credits.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Orchestrate conversation distribution with natural language playbooks.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Use bullseye routing with user groups to orchestrate conversations
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to Use bullseye routing with user groups to orchestrate conversations in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability by November 6, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature introduces a tiered assignment strategy that automatically expands the pool of eligible customer service representatives as conversation wait times increase. Admins can configure a bullseye routing playbook, allowing them to associate user groups with a queue and define wait time thresholds for each tier they add to that queue. Once configured, conversation orchestration monitors each conversation's wait time and automatically expands the eligible pool when thresholds are reached.

What action do I need to take?
Admins can enable bullseye routing under conversation orchestration to start configuring bullseye playbooks. If you’re already using bullseye routing under conversation orchestration, you can continue using your existing configurations without additional action.

Copilot credits are used only when an admin publishes a playbook, which makes the configured orchestration logic active for use. Once published, the playbook can process any number of customer conversations without consuming additional Copilot credits. Saving a playbook as a draft or simply enabling Conversation Orchestration does not consume Copilot credits.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Use bullseye routing with user groups to orchestrate conversations.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: New ways to work across Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why:]

We are evolving Microsoft Copilot to better connect the tools people rely on with the capablities they need to build, customize, and scale AI across work. Updates include a new Home experience and enhanced Office capabilities in the Copilot app; Code and Autopilot for building solutions and automating work; an enterprise-grade platform for running code; and updates to Copilot Notebooks, Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive, and Work IQ.

[Impact on your organization:]

Home in the Copilot app:

  • When users open the Copilot app, they will land in Home, which brings Chat and Cowork together on one screen. Users can switch between Chat and Cowork in the prompt box. Read more in the blog. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • As part of this update, we are making the following updates to the left navigation pane: 1) Agents & Plugins will replace the standalone Agents entry point (called Agents & Skills for some preview users) from Chat and the Customize entry point from Cowork. 2) For users with access to Cowork, Automations from Cowork will move to the Home navigation pane. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • Researcher and Analyst will no longer be pinned by default in the Copilot app navigation pane. Users can continue to access these agents from Plugins and can pin them to the navigation pane based on their preferences. Organizations that want these agents to remain pinned for their users can pre-pin them through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Chat can complete long-running, multi-step knowledge work, including drafting email, managing meetings, working in Teams, managing OneDrive and SharePoint files, finding people, and creating Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and HTML files. Sensitive actions require user approval. Users can track and manage their long-running activity from Chat in the Tasks view, accessible in the upper right of the Copilot app navigation pane. These capabilities will roll out to Frontier later this month and are available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Chat will begin surfacing Skills that are used while generating responses, giving users greater transparency into how Copilot responds. This update will begin worldwide rollout in October and is available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Code:

  • The new Code experience gives users a dedicated place in the Copilot app to create trackers, dashboards, and apps using natural language. Users can access Code by going to the Code tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Code uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • Code is rolling out to Frontier later this month.
  • To prepare: To enable Copilot Code for your tenant, admin must deploy the unified app and set the target channel to beta.

Autopilot:

  • Autopilot, previously called Scout, is an always-on personal agent in the Copilot app with persistent context, identity, and memory. Users can access Autopilot by going to the Autopilot tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Autopilot uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • We will update this message with rollout timing and admin control details when available.

Copilot app UI updates:

  • Cowork, Code, and Autopilot entry points in the Copilot app will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Users that do not have a spending policy enabled will not be able to access these capabilities; instead, they will see an in-product message after clicking on the entry points to request access or learn more.
  • A new Microsoft 365 admin center setting will let admins choose whether users without a spending policy see Request Access or Learn More. Admins can configure whether or not users can request Copilot credits to use these experiences. Admins can also choose to block requests.
  • The existing setting in the admin center used to hide usage-based experiences (“Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing”) will be removed.
  • By default, enterprise users without a spending policy will see the “request access” message. Education users will see a Learn More link and cannot request access.
  • This update will roll out to standard customers in October and deferred customers in November.
  • To prepare: Review Microsoft 365 Admin center settings for usage-based experiences and spending policy. Decide if you want users without a spending policy to receive a "Request access" or "Learn more" message.

Full Office capabilities in the Copilot app:

  • Users can use full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint creation, editing, and collaboration capabilities in the Copilot app, side by side with Copilot. Users can also access recent Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files from Library in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Capabilities accessed through Chat are included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license. Capabilities accessed through Cowork use usage-based billing.
  • These capabilities are rolling out to Frontier later this month.

Copilot Managed Runtime:

  • Copilot Managed Runtime is an enterprise-grade platform for running code within the Microsoft 365 tenant boundary under IT governance. It supports apps built in Code, Cowork, Copilot Studio, and supported command-line and SDK experiences. Admins can manage these apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Read more in the blog.
  • Managed Runtime is starting to roll out now into public preview.

Copilot Notebooks updates:

  • Copilot Notebooks will add task delegation, full Office editing and collaboration, interactive report creation, audio overview updates, model selection, and an updated user experience in the Copilot app and OneNote.
  • These updates will roll out to Frontier later this month.

SharePoint and OneDrive updates:

  • We are announcing the general availability of Copilot in SharePoint. The everyday AI capabilities that have been in public preview stay included with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). New agentic capabilities and the ability to work at greater scale than was possible in preview will be available through usage-based billing (UBB) and consume Copilot Credits. We are also introducing general availability of Copilot in OneDrive, which follows the same licensing structure as SharePoint. Read more about Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive in the blog.
  • General availability begins rolling out later this month. Tenant availability may follow as rollout progresses.
  • To prepare: No action is required to continue using capabilities included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). Admins can control who can access advanced SharePoint capabilities through UBB by going to Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management. Existing cost management policies may automatically include newly available services. Existing PowerShell opt-out settings for the Public Preview of Copilot in SharePoint will continue to be honored until November 1st; after that, manage availability through SharePoint site AI settings.

Business Applications in Work IQ:

  • Work IQ now includes Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and Power Platform data, enabling Copilot to ground responses and tasks on business and productivity data. Read more in the blog.
  • These updates will start rolling out in public preview later this month.
  • To prepare: Admins can configure Dynamics 365 and Power Platform data sources for Copilot in the Power Platform admin center. Admins can also manage the availability of business applications in Copilot in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings, and access through the Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) under Agents > Tools.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

In addition to the guidance listed in the individual updates above:

  • A spending policy is required for users to access capabilities available through Usage-based billing. Enable Copilot Credit consumption and configure spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Cost management. Educate users about usage-based billing scenarios and how to request access through IT. Learn more about spending policy and usage-based billing in the blog and message center post titled: Evolving Copilot pricing and new FinOps capabilities for AI.
  • Monitor this post for updated availability and deployment details.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Enhanced Copilot and AI controls for meetings
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams is updating how administrators and meeting organizers configure AI for Teams meetings. The existing Copilot meeting policy is being replaced by two more specific policies:

  • MeetingAI - controls whether Copilot, Facilitator, Intelligent Recap, and other AI features are available in meetings.
  • TranscriptionWithMeetingAI - controls whether transcription starts automatically when meeting AI is turned on.

This gives administrators clearer, more predictable control over whether AI is available and whether it requires (or works without) transcription, including the ability to enforce Copilot off. Organizers also gain more visibility into, and in some cases control over, these settings directly from the meeting options.

Meeting options are also being updated to make AI controls easier to understand and to provide more granular control over who can enable, manage, and use AI capabilities, including a new who can manage option that replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator meeting option:

  • Who can manage AI - replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator option and determines who can turn Copilot and other AI features on or off during a meeting. If an admin turns Meeting AI off, this option is set to No one.
  • Who can use AI - provides more granular control over which meeting participants can use Copilot and other AI capabilities.
  • Start Transcription with AI - lets organizers choose whether transcription starts with AI. Administrators can also control this option through Teams admin center.
  • Intelligent Recap controls - lets organizers decide whether an Intelligent Recap is created when Copilot is turned on, including for meetings where a transcript is not created.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 (previously mid-November) and expect to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously early December).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early January 2027 (previously late November 2026) and expect to complete by mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Today, the Copilot policy combines whether AI is available in a meeting with whether a saved transcript is required. After this update, these behaviors are represented by two separate settings:

  • Allow AI in meetings: On / Off, but organizers can change / Off, and organizers cannot change
  • Start transcription when AI is turned on: On, but organizers can change / On, and organizers cannot change / Off

To keep the experience predictable and avoid invalid combinations: if MeetingAI is set to enforced off, transcription will also be turned off; if transcription is then turned back on, MeetingAI will no longer be enforced off.

In PowerShell, administrators will use MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI instead of the existing Copilot policy. Once the new controls are enabled, the Copilot policy can no longer be updated directly - attempts will return guidance to use the new policies.

What happens to existing configurations: Microsoft will perform a one-time update mapping each existing Copilot value to the corresponding MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI values, preserving the current effective behavior for your organization. Administrators do not need to recreate their policies. Examples include:

Copilot is on and uses a saved transcript by defaultOnOn, but organizers can change
Copilot is on and a saved transcript is requiredOnOn, and organizers cannot change
Copilot is available without transcriptionOnOff
Copilot is off, but organizers can enable itOff, but organizers can changeBased on the existing transcription configuration
Copilot is enforced offOff, and organizers cannot changeOff
Existing configurationMeetingAITranscriptionWithMeetingAI

The Transcription policy remains available and continues to control whether transcription is allowed. The new TranscriptionWithMeetingAI policy controls whether transcription starts when meeting AI is turned on.

The new settings will appear in the Teams admin center meeting policy under Recording and transcription and Copilot and other AI.

[Insert provided Teams admin center screenshot here]

The screenshot shows the new Start transcription when AI is turned on control and Allow AI in all meetings control, including the options administrators can use to set defaults or prevent organizers from changing the configured behavior.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required to migrate existing configurations. Before rollout, we recommend admins:

  • Review any automation or scripts that read or update the Copilot meeting policy, and update them to use MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI.
  • Review custom tooling, runbooks, or documentation referencing the Copilot policy.
  • Inform Teams administrators that existing behavior will now be represented by two settings in Teams admin center.
  • Confirm the mapped configuration reflects intended behavior once the new controls are available.

If you do not use PowerShell or custom automation to manage Teams meeting policies, no action is required. Existing configurations will be mapped automatically.

[Compliance considerations:]

This change affects administrative controls over AI and transcription availability in meetings but does not alter how existing customer data is processed or stored. Review AI and transcription governance policies for your organization as appropriate.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: New experience when users minimize the meeting window
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

We are improving the Microsoft Teams meeting experience when the active meeting window is minimized. This update helps users stay engaged in meetings while multitasking across other apps. With this change, users can perform key in-meeting actions—such as raising their hand and sending reactions—without restoring the full Teams meeting window. Users can also choose between two different minimized views, depending on how much meeting context they want to keep visible while they work.

This change does not affect the experience when users are sharing their screen in a Teams meeting.

This message applies to Teams for Windows desktop and Teams for Mac desktop. It is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557179.

[When this will happen:]

  • Targeted Release: Rollout begins mid-May 2026 (previously early May) and is expected to complete by late May 2026 (previously early May).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We expect to complete rollout by end of November 2026 (previously end of October). 

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • All users who join and participate in Microsoft Teams meetings.

What will happen:

  • When users minimize a Teams meeting window, a new minimized meeting experience appears automatically.
  • Users can raise their hand and send reactions without restoring the full Microsoft Teams meeting window.
  • Users can choose between two minimized views:
    • Expanded view: Displays up to four participant videos.
    • Compact view: Does not display participant video and takes up less screen space.
  • The feature is enabled by default and does not require any admin configuration.
  • There is no change to the meeting experience while screen sharing.

[What you can do to prepare:]

  • No action is required.
  • Consider notifying users and helpdesk staff about the new minimized meeting views in Microsoft Teams.
  • Update internal training or support documentation if it references Teams meeting window behavior.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

  • Event producers who use NDI streaming in Microsoft Teams meetings and events

Platforms and services

  • To access the feature during a meeting or event, select More actions, then Streaming > Streaming switchboard.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Onboarding workflow for new team members
item.description:

[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams is introducing an onboarding workflow that helps new team members get started faster by automatically connecting them to relevant channels when they join a team. This can improve engagement, accelerate onboarding, and make important information easier to find from the start.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 573452.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expect to complete in mid-November 2026 (previously early November).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Today, new team members may need to manually discover and join the channels that are most relevant to their work. With this update, team owners can automatically add new members to relevant channels through the onboarding workflow when they are added to a team.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required. You may want to inform team owners about this upcoming improvement so they understand how to connect new members to relevant channels more efficiently during onboarding.
